summary.description: Arsenic is a grey solid element with both metallic and non-metallic properties. Its inorganic compounds are usually colourless solids, with varying solubility in water.
emission_sources: Burning of fossil fuels in power stations
Use in agricultural pesticides and wood preservatives
Natural occurrence in soils, rocks, and groundwater
environmental_impact: Persists in the environment and accumulates in living organisms
Toxic to wildlife at high concentrations
Long-term human exposure may cause skin and lung cancer, along with irritation from skin contact

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Arsenic exposure is linked to serious long-term health effects including cancer, making it a major public health concern in both urban and rural areas.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Arsenic naturally contaminates groundwater in many regions, posing risks to safe drinking water and sanitation goals.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: Due to its persistence and bioaccumulation, arsenic is highly toxic to terrestrial wildlife and contributes to soil degradation and biodiversity loss.
